The automations that keep the blueprint still update when the blueprint does; the ones you took control of do not, which is fine, they are two lines long.

docs.title: Rain Bird
docs.text:
• Controller zone entity: the zone's switch (one is created for every zone on the controller).
  • Turn off its schedule: in the Rain Bird app, disable each program, or remove every watering day from it. Do not put the controller's dial on OFF: on most models that blocks every run, including the ones started from the app or from Home Assistant.
  • The integration polls the controller once a minute, so the zone's state in Home Assistant can lag the valve by up to a minute. That matters only for observed watering, not for the blueprint.

docs.title: Hunter Hydrawise
docs.text:
• Controller zone entity: the zone's binary sensor that shows whether it is watering (device class running), not a switch. That is the entity the hydrawise.start_watering action targets, and the blueprint's list is filtered to it.
  • Turn off its schedule: every zone has an auto_watering switch in Home Assistant. Turning it off suspends the zone's Smart Watering schedule for a year (that is how the integration implements it), while runs started from Home Assistant still work. You can also suspend the zone in the Hydrawise app.

docs.title: Rachio
docs.text:
• Controller zone entity: the zone's switch.
  • Turn off its schedule: each Rachio schedule is a switch in Home Assistant, turn the ones that cover the zone off, or disable them in the Rachio app.
  • The 3 hour cap is Rachio's, see above.
  • Rachio updates Home Assistant through the cloud: the integration's page explains that your Home Assistant must be reachable from the internet for zone states to update. The blueprint does not depend on that (it waits the duration it asked for), observed watering does.
  • The integration's option "duration in minutes when activating a zone switch" is a failsafe for the switch. The blueprint passes its own duration to the action and does not use it.

docs.title: OpenSprinkler
docs.text:
• Controller zone entity: the station's enabled switch (the integration marks it with device class station; the blueprint's list is filtered to those). It is the entity the opensprinkler.run_station action takes, and the station must be enabled or the run is refused.
  • Turn off its schedule: each OpenSprinkler program has an enabled switch in Home Assistant, turn them off, or disable the programs in the OpenSprinkler interface. Keep the controller's own enabled switch on.
  • Runs are queued, so several zones asked at once water one after the other.
  • The blueprint calls opensprinkler.run_station. An older copy calls opensprinkler.run, which the integration has deprecated: if yours does, import the blueprint again.

docs.title: Orbit B-hyve
docs.text:
• Controller zone entity: the zone's valve entity (a switch on older versions of the integration).
  • Turn off its schedule: in Home Assistant, turn off the zone's smart watering switch and each program switch that includes the zone, or do the same in the B-hyve app.
  • The integration recommends bhyve.start_watering with a number of minutes over opening the valve, because some devices cannot set a default watering time. That is what the blueprint uses.

docs.title: Telling us how it went
docs.text: Each blueprint says in its description that it is not yet confirmed on real hardware. When you have run one, please post in the discussions: the controller model, whether the zone started and stopped at the right time, and anything you had to change. Once a controller is confirmed we remove the warning from its blueprint.

docs.title: Other irrigation integrations
docs.text:
With Calculate only, Smart Irrigation can hand its calculated run times to another integration that drives the valves: Irrigation Unlimited or Irrigation-V5. This page says how. For the controllers of Rain Bird, Hydrawise, Rachio, OpenSprinkler and B-hyve, see off-the-shelf controllers.

To let Smart Irrigation run the valves itself instead, with programs and schedules, see Watering with programs, and Coming from Irrigation Unlimited to import an Irrigation Unlimited configuration.

docs.title: Irrigation Unlimited
docs.text:
Smart Irrigation calculates how long each zone should water, and Irrigation Unlimited (IU) runs the valves. The two do not talk to each other directly: the duration is handed over by a blueprint or an automation that calls IU's own adjust_time action. There is nothing to enable in either integration, and no configuration.yaml block to add for Smart Irrigation, which is set up in the interface only (adding one causes a setup error on restart).

Use the adjust time blueprint that matches your setup (a zone of its own, or a zone inside a sequence), together with the reset bucket one. Either way it is one automation per zone: a sequence adjusted as a whole spreads the time you give it across its zones in proportion to their original durations, so a calculated duration handed to the sequence would water every zone by the wrong amount.

IU exposes binary_sensor entities, not switches. Do not drive the valve yourself in parallel, or the two will fight. An automation of your own looks like this:

alias: "Smart Irrigation to IU: duration of zone 1"
triggers:
  - trigger: time
    at: "23:00:00"
conditions:
  - condition: template
    value_template: "{{ states('sensor.smart_irrigation_zone_1') | int(0) > 0 }}"
actions:
  - action: irrigation_unlimited.adjust_time
    data:
      entity_id: binary_sensor.irrigation_unlimited_c1_z1
      actual: "{{ timedelta(seconds=states('sensor.smart_irrigation_zone_1') | int(0)) }}"

The water balance can be credited by a separate automation that triggers when the IU zone turns off: see the Irrigation Unlimited reset blueprint in the blueprints table, or observed watering on the valve IU drives.

If IU does not get the duration, check that the blueprint or automation runs, and that its IU entity exists (a binary_sensor).

The sync services are gone

sync_with_irrigation_unlimited, send_zone_data_to_irrigation_unlimited and get_irrigation_unlimited_status have been removed. They belonged to a sync subsystem that was switched off and had no setting to switch it on: the flag it read was never a setting of this integration, so it could not work for anyone, and calling one returned quietly with a warning in the log (discussion #696). It also guessed which IU entity belonged to which zone from their names. The blueprint replaces them.

docs.title: Irrigation-V5
docs.text:
Irrigation-V5 is another scheduler and controller. Like Irrigation Unlimited it does not calculate anything, so Smart Irrigation supplies the run time and V5 runs the valves.

No automation is needed for this one. V5 reads a numeric entity as a multiplier on a zone's watering time, and its author documents the way to turn that into "run for exactly this many seconds":

  1. In the zone's advanced options, set the watering unit to seconds.
  2. Set the zone's watering time to 1.
  3. Set the zone's Adjustment Sensor to the Smart Irrigation sensor of that zone, sensor.smart_irrigation_[zone_name].

V5 then runs for 1 x the value of our sensor seconds, which is the calculated duration. When Smart Irrigation says no watering is needed, the sensor reads 0, the multiplier is 0, and V5 skips the zone: whether to water and for how long both come from the calculation.

Keep the duration sensor in seconds

It has a duration device class, so Home Assistant lets you change the unit it shows per entity. Switching it to minutes would make V5 read minutes as if they were seconds, and water for a sixtieth of the time.

docs.title: Crediting the water balance with Irrigation-V5
docs.text:
V5 drives your own valve or solenoid entity, so Smart Irrigation can watch that same entity: turn on observed watering and set the zone's Linked valve/switch to the valve V5 operates (see closed loop). The water balance is then credited from the run that actually happened, with no automation.

To stay open loop, call smart_irrigation.credit_watering from your own automation when the valve turns off, and do not turn on observed watering as well, or the water is credited twice.

docs.title: Seasonal adjustments and recurring schedules
docs.text:
Seasonal adjustments scale the crop factor and shift the irrigation threshold over a range of months. They are set on the advanced panel or with smart_irrigation.set_seasonal_adjustment: see seasonal adjustments.

action: smart_irrigation.set_seasonal_adjustment
data:
  name: "Summer boost"
  month_start: 6  # June
  month_end: 8    # August
  multiplier_adjustment: 1.3
  threshold_adjustment: -5.0
  zones: "all"
  enabled: true

Without adjustment_id it creates an adjustment; with it, it changes that one, and with remove: true as well it removes it. A calculation of a zone that an adjustment covers fires smart_irrigation_seasonal_adjustment_applied (zone_id, adjustments).

Recurring schedules are on their way out

create_recurring_schedule, update_recurring_schedule and delete_recurring_schedule keep working until version 2027.11 at the earliest, and each call raises a repair issue. The programs' schedules do the same, in the panel, under Watering › Programs (Calculate and water). See actions on their way out.

A recurring schedule runs daily, weekly, monthly or every few hours, and either calculates (calculate), reads the weather (update) or fires the start event (irrigate) for the zones it names. It fires smart_irrigation_recurring_schedule_triggered. For their debug log:

logger:
  logs:
    custom_components.smart_irrigation.scheduler: debug

docs.title: Entities
docs.text:
Each zone has a duration sensor in Home Assistant, named sensor.smart_irrigation_[zone_name]: a zone called "Lawn" has sensor.smart_irrigation_lawn. Its state is the watering duration in seconds.

Its attributes:

Attribute Description id internal identification size the area the zone waters, in m² or sq ft. throughput the flow of the zone, in litres or gallons per minute. input_method how the precipitation rate is determined: throughput (from size + throughput) or direct (entered directly). precipitation_rate the directly entered precipitation rate in mm/h or in/h, when input_method is direct. state automatic, manual or disabled. bucket the water balance, in mm or inch. The attribute keeps the name bucket, as do maximum_bucket and the entity ids ending in _bucket, so automations keep working. bucket_unit, size_unit, throughput_unit, drainage_rate_unit, current_drainage_unit, maximum_bucket_unit, precipitation_rate_unit, et_value_unit, et_deficiency_unit, eto_unit the unit each figure is shown in, following the unit system of Home Assistant (mm or inch, m² or sq ft, litres or gallons per minute). multiplier the zone's crop factor (Kc). lead_time the lead time of the zone, in seconds. maximum_duration the maximum duration of a run for the zone, in seconds. drainage_rate how fast a saturated root zone drains, per hour (see drainage_rate_unit). current_drainage the water drained at the last calculation. maximum_bucket the most water the root zone holds above field capacity. last_updated when weather data was last retrieved for the zone. last_calculated when the zone was last calculated. number_of_data_points how many readings the last calculation worked from. et_value the net precipitation applied to the water balance by the last calculation, in mm or inch: the water need over the interval with the precipitation already subtracted from it. It is positive on a day where more rain fell than water evaporated. Despite its name this is not the evapotranspiration. et_deficiency what this zone needs, per day, before the interval scaling and before precipitation, in mm or inch. Negative, because it is what the soil lost. It carries the zone's crop factor, so it is ETc = ET0 x Kc and it agrees with the water balance beside it. Unlike the water balance it does not depend on the calculation interval or on water balance resets, so this is the value to compare when trying out configurations. eto the reference evapotranspiration of the same run, positive, with no crop factor. This is the number the literature and the weather services quote, so it is the one to hold against an external ET0 figure. unit_of_measurement seconds. device_class duration. icon mdi:sprinkler by default. friendly_name the name of your zone.

Most attributes also have an entity of their own, below. For another one, a template sensor can read it, for example the water balance:

{{ state_attr('sensor.smart_irrigation_lawn', 'bucket') }}

docs.title: Per-zone device and entities
docs.text:
Each zone is also grouped as a device in Home Assistant (named after the zone), attached to the single Smart Irrigation hub device. Alongside the duration sensor above, the device exposes dedicated entities, so a zone reads as a set of entities rather than one attribute bag:

Entity Type Description Duration (sensor.smart_irrigation_[zone]) sensor Calculated watering duration (seconds). This is the original entity: its entity_id, recorded history and attributes are preserved. Water balance sensor Current soil water balance (mm/inch); negative means deficit. This is the value the last calculation committed. Live water balance sensor Where the zone stands now: the same calculation run over the readings collected since the last one, without committing anything. Recomputed as the zone's readings arrive, at most every thirty seconds. Its live attribute is false when there is nothing to estimate from yet (just after a calculation), and the value is then the committed water balance; since, as_of and duration say what the estimate covers and the run it implies. Applied ET sensor The same figure as the et_value attribute: the net precipitation applied to the water balance at the last calculation (the water need over the interval, et0 x interval, with the rain already subtracted). Positive when more rain fell than water evaporated. Despite its name it is not the evapotranspiration; for that see Daily ET deficiency and the eto attribute. Diagnostic, disabled on a new zone. Daily ET deficiency sensor This zone's daily need, crop factor included, independent of the interval and of rain. The et_deficiency attribute of the duration sensor. Diagnostic, disabled on a new zone. Current drainage sensor Water drained as runoff at the last calculation. The current_drainage attribute of the duration sensor. Diagnostic, disabled on a new zone. Last irrigation sensor (timestamp) When the zone was last credited for a run. Water used sensor (water, total) Cumulative water delivered to the zone (litres). Last run volume sensor (water) The water the zone's last credited run delivered (litres). Next irrigation sensor (timestamp) When the zone is watered next, as the panel says. Unknown when no run to come waters it; a run the weather would hold back as things stand is still its next run, with the attribute skip_expected saying so. Multiplier number Editable per-zone crop factor, written to the store and used by the next calculation. Listed under Configuration. Irrigation needed binary_sensor On when the water balance is in deficit. Watering now binary_sensor On while the zone's linked valve/switch is open. Problem binary_sensor On when a valve problem was reported (e.g. it never opened); clears on the next successful run. Calculate button Recalculate this zone now. Reset water balance button Set the water balance to 0 ("I just watered, start from zero"). Reset water usage button Zero the cumulative water-used counter. Irrigate now button Run this zone's valve for its calculated duration (only shown with Calculate and water). The run credits the water balance, so the delivered water is accounted for and the next calculation irrigates less. The zone (valve.smart_irrigation_[zone]) valve The zone as a water valve, for dashboards, voice assistants and valve.open_valve / valve.close_valve. Open waters the zone for its calculated duration, like Irrigate now and water_zone: behind a run in progress it takes its turn, and the run credits the water balance. Close stops the zone's watering, and closes its valve when something else had opened it. It shows open or closed as the linked valve does. Available with Calculate and water when the zone has a linked valve.

Diagnostic, configuration, disabled. Applied ET, Daily ET deficiency and Current drainage repeat an attribute of the duration sensor that few dashboards show, so they are diagnostic entities and a zone created since 2026.11 has them disabled: enable one in its entity settings when you want it. A zone that already had them keeps them as they were. The Multiplier is a setting and is listed under Configuration, as are the hub's Skip on precipitation and Precipitation threshold. Home Assistant leaves diagnostic and configuration entities out of the dashboards it generates; a dashboard of your own can show them like any other.

docs.title: Hub device
docs.text:
The Smart Irrigation hub device carries the entities of the whole installation:

  • the buttons Calculate all zones, Refresh weather, and, with Calculate and water, Irrigate all zones;
  • the binary sensors A zone needs water and Problem (on while any zone's own is on), Leak (see water flowing with every valve closed) and Observed watering (on while observed watering is);
  • the switch Calculate and water (switch.smart_irrigation_irrigation_enabled): off, nothing is calculated and nothing is watered (see Stop everything). It stays on with Calculate only (see What Smart Irrigation does). It also has a switch, Skip on precipitation, and a number, Precipitation threshold, both under Configuration: the rain forecast skip of the Skip watering page, which you can change from an automation or a dashboard. The number is in mm, or inch with the imperial unit system.

Postponing from a dashboard. The hub device also has two buttons, Postpone watering 24 h and Postpone watering 48 h, a Resume watering button, and a datetime entity, Watering postponed until (datetime.smart_irrigation_postponed_until). The datetime shows the end of the postponement in force, or nothing, and setting it holds the watering back until that moment: a date and time for the end of your holidays, for instance, from a dashboard or an automation. A moment already past lifts the postponement. They all do what the postpone_irrigation and resume_irrigation actions do, and what Hold for 24 h, Hold for 48 h and Resume now on the Info page do.

docs.title: Program sensors
docs.text:
With Calculate and water, each program has one sensor on the hub device: sensor.smart_irrigation_program_<id>, named "Program ". A program that is added gets its sensor, and one that is deleted loses it. The state is one of idle, waiting, running, paused or suspended. The attributes: Attribute Description program_id the id of the program, which is also in the entity id. next_start the next time a schedule starts it, or empty. last_run when it last started. suspended_until the end of its suspension, or empty. adjustment the adjust_program adjustment in force (percent, seconds and until), or empty. manual while it waits or runs: true when it was asked for by hand rather than by a schedule. tour, tours while it runs: the round it is on and how many rounds it has (both count from 1; tour is 0 while it waits). step, steps while it runs: the step it is on and how many steps the round has (step is 0 while it waits). percent while it runs: how far along it is, 0 to 100. remaining_seconds while it runs: the time left, paused time excluded.

The attributes from manual down are only there while the program waits or runs.

A program has no on and off switch of its own: it starts on its own through its schedules that are on. To keep one from watering (say, for the holidays), switch its schedules off with set_schedule_enabled, or suspend it. The program switch entities of 2026.11.0 are gone; the migration switched off the schedules of a program that was off.

The per-zone entities are additive: nothing was removed. The duration sensor keeps its entity_id, recorded history and attributes, so existing dashboards, automations and templates keep working. A one-time registry migration moves the duration sensor's internal unique_id to a stable per-zone scheme; the entity_id and history carry over.

The per-zone device/entity layout is inspired by JustChr's Smart Irrigation fork (MIT).

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Smart Irrigation fires these events on the Home Assistant event bus:

Event Description smart_irrigation_start_irrigation_all_zones With Calculate only, fired when the active start trigger is reached and the run is not held back. Listen to it to start your watering: see automations. With Calculate and water, it also fires when a schedule starts the program with the id main (the former main program, now Watering; trigger_type is then program), so automations written for it keep working. That last use goes in 2027.11 (see no main program). smart_irrigation_irrigation_skipped Fired when a start (a program's schedule, or a start trigger) is held back by the skip conditions, so nothing is watered at that start. Data: the identity of what started (for a program, program_id and schedule_id), plus reason and checks, the same detail the Home page shows. The reason is the check that held the start back: postponed, rain_sensor, freeze, wind, precipitation, days_between or soil_moisture. A trigger reached while Smart Irrigation is stopped fires it with the reason irrigation_off (and no checks). smart_irrigation_leak Fired when a zone's meter counts water with every valve closed, with Leak alert after set. Data: flow_sensor, litres, zone_ids, zones. smart_irrigation_weather_stale A temperature, humidity, dew point, wind speed or pressure source of a sensor group has not reported for 6 hours; fired once per silence. Data: mapping_id, mapping, fields (the fields that just went silent) and since (the time of the last report). See silent sensors. smart_irrigation_weather_recovered Fields that were silent report again, or the outage stops being watched. Data: mapping_id, mapping, fields, and reason when it is not a recovery: unloaded (the integration was reloaded, disabled or removed) or unwatched (no automatic zone uses the group any more).

When Smart Irrigation waters (Calculate and water), it fires more:

  • smart_irrigation_irrigation_started, smart_irrigation_irrigation_finished and smart_irrigation_zone_problem, described in closed-loop watering;
  • smart_irrigation_program_started, program_finished, valve_on, valve_off, valve_out_of_sync and supply_problem, described in seeing what is going on;
  • smart_irrigation_zone_unwatered: a zone has been dry for more than 3 days and no program will water it; fired once per zone, together with a repair notice. Data: zone_id, zone, days, deficit_mm. See the dry zone notice.

Every event, with its data, is also listed on one page: the output contract.

docs.title: Knowing a run was skipped
docs.text:
A skipped day used to be the absence of an event, and nothing can listen for something that does not happen. That is why a skip fires its own event:

alias: Tell me when watering was skipped
triggers:
  - trigger: event
    event_type: smart_irrigation_irrigation_skipped
actions:
  - action: notify.persistent_notification
    data:
      message: "No watering today: {{ trigger.event.data.reason }}"

The Home page answers the same question without an automation: it shows whether the next start would be skipped and why, and what the last real decision was.

docs.title: The start event
docs.text: With Calculate only, smart_irrigation_start_irrigation_all_zones fires when the active start trigger is reached: the default (done by sunrise), a trigger you added, or none at all. How to choose it, and what Account for duration does, is under start triggers. The skip conditions still apply: when they hold a start back, the start event is not fired, and the skipped event above is fired instead.

docs.title: Event data
docs.text:
The event carries the identity of the trigger that fired, so one automation can react differently per trigger:

Field Meaning trigger_name the name you gave the trigger trigger_type sunrise, sunset, solar_azimuth or time. For a start of the program main (Calculate and water), program, with program_id and schedule_id too at for a time trigger, the clock time it is set to offset_minutes the configured offset, in minutes account_for_duration whether timing is shifted so watering finishes at the target moment

Example: filter on trigger_name to react to one trigger.

triggers:
  - trigger: event
    event_type: smart_irrigation_start_irrigation_all_zones
    event_data:
      trigger_name: "Morning"

docs.title: Coming from Irrigation Unlimited
docs.text:
Irrigation Unlimited (IU) is a scheduler and a sequencer of valves with no water model: it does not know the weather, the evapotranspiration or how much water a zone has lost. Smart Irrigation does, and the two used to be joined by two automations written by hand (adjust_time into IU, reset_bucket at the end).

With Calculate and water, Smart Irrigation does the scheduling and the running itself, with its programs. This page says where each thing you used in IU went. It can also bring your configuration over for you: see Importing your configuration.

docs.title: The words
docs.text: In Irrigation Unlimited In Smart Irrigation Controller (and its master entity) Supply: a pump or a main valve, with a delay before and after that can be negative Zone Zone, with its linked valve (and, if it needs several, other valves) Sequence Program Sequence zone (a step) Step: one zone, or several watered together Step with zones in parallel A step with several zones, watered at the same time Delay between steps, including a negative one Wait after this step; a negative value overlaps the steps (up to an hour) adjust_time (actual, percentage, increase, decrease) The step's duration: calculated (the default), calculated times a percentage, or fixed, with a minimum, a maximum (min_seconds, max_seconds) and an offset in seconds (adjust_seconds: -120, YAML only, see YAML-only options). For a temporary change of a whole program, smart_irrigation.adjust_program (a percent and/or seconds, for some hours or until reset). You no longer need an automation to hand it the duration, because the calculated one is the default. reset_bucket or set_bucket after the run Nothing to do: a run of ours credits the water balance itself, for the water that went through suspend smart_irrigation.suspend, for a zone or a program, for some hours or until a date manual_run smart_irrigation.water_zone or smart_irrigation.run_program. A manual run joins the queue and takes its turn by default (mode: queue); mode: replace stops what is running first. run_program also takes seconds, a total shared between the steps, and stop_program ends one program. cancel smart_irrigation.stop_watering Pause and resume smart_irrigation.pause_watering and resume_watering Skip to the next step smart_irrigation.next_step Schedule (time, sun, cron) A program's schedules: time of day or sun (with an offset, and a fallback time for polar days, fallback_time: previous, YAML only, see YAML-only options), with the days as filters. Cron is not supported as such; the import turns a cron line with a bounded set of times into time schedules. anchor: start and anchor: finish The schedule's moment is when the program starts, or when it must be done (the start is worked back from the length of the run) Weekdays, day of the month, even/odd, every_n_days, months, from/to The same filters, on each schedule: days of the week, every N days, and a period of the year that may span New Year, in the form; the shift of every N days (every_offset: 1), even or odd days (parity: even), named days of the month (days_of_month: [1, 15, last]) and months (months: [5, 6, 7, 8, 9]) are YAML only, see YAML-only options entity_states Not the same feature. In IU it lets a timed valve receive only the on command, only the off, or neither. We have no such switch. The nearest things are the per-zone safety off mode (auto, zha, off), which can arm a hardware timed off (MQTT topic, or a ZHA command) as a dead-man behind the normal close, the Valve's own duration of a valve that closes by itself, and the check while a valve is open. See hardware auto-off. check_back (delay, retries) The zone's Wait for the valve to confirm (advanced mode) and how often the open is sent again (open_resends, YAML only: the zone's Edit in YAML). The wait applies to the open and the close. A valve that closes by itself while it should be open is caught by the check every 60 seconds and is not reopened (see sync_error below) irrigation_unlimited_start and finish events smart_irrigation_program_started and program_finished valve_on and valve_off events smart_irrigation_valve_on and valve_off, for zones and supplies sync_error smart_irrigation_valve_out_of_sync, with a smart_irrigation_zone_problem of reason valve_closed_early: a valve held open that reads closed switch_error smart_irrigation_zone_problem (a zone valve) and supply_problem (a pump or main valve)

docs.title: What is different
docs.text:
• Programs never overlap. IU lets overlapping runs go on together; here a second program waits for the first, and a step with several zones (or a negative wait between steps) is how you ask for zones at the same time. A pump on a home network seldom has the pressure for more.
  • The weather is part of the schedule. A schedule skips, shortens or holds back what the skip conditions say. Turn it off per schedule if you want a plain timer.
  • The default duration is the one Smart Irrigation calculated, not a number you type.
  • No YAML file to maintain. It is all in the panel; a few power-user options are written in a program's or a zone's Edit in YAML (see YAML-only options). A restart goes on with the steps still to do instead of dropping a run that was under way.

docs.title: Importing your configuration
docs.text:
Under Settings › General, the card Import from Irrigation Unlimited opens a wizard that reads your IU configuration and turns it into zones, programs, their schedules and supplies. It takes the configuration from where IU has it: your YAML (configuration.yaml and its includes, as Home Assistant loaded it), IU's own settings when it was set up in the interface, or YAML you paste. Pasted YAML is read as text: !include, !secret and !env_var are not followed, and the report says so.

Nothing is changed before you have seen it all:

  1. Zones: each IU zone is matched to one of your zones (by the one you choose, then by its valve, the blueprint that feeds it, or its name) or created. A zone you already have keeps its settings and only gets the fields it had empty.
  2. Programs and supplies: what each IU sequence and controller becomes, step by step. A sequence fed by Smart Irrigation's durations (an adjust-time automation) waters the calculated duration; the others keep IU's fixed times. The automation may adjust the sequence (with its zones) or each zone's own entity (binary_sensor.irrigation_unlimited_c1_z1, …): IU applies a zone's adjustment inside every sequence that waters it, so a step whose zones are all fed that way is calculated too.
  3. The report: what was carried over exactly, what was approximated (a cron expression turned into times, for example) and what has no equivalent here.

The schedules of new programs are created switched off, so IU keeps watering until you are ready to switch over. The wizard says so differently when IU is not running, for instance because Home Assistant rejected its configuration: nothing waters then until you switch the schedules on.

The programs need Calculate and water. Choosing it creates a program with every zone that has a valve when there is no program yet. If you import first, the imported programs are the ones that water: a program only waters the zones of its steps. A program of your own that waters the same zones as the imported ones waters them twice: switch its schedules off under Watering › Programs. Importing again later updates what the earlier import made, in place, and removes what IU no longer has; the wizard asks before it removes anything. Only an administrator can import.

docs.title: Switching over
docs.text:
At the top of the import page, once something is imported:

  • Switch over to Smart Irrigation switches off IU's controllers that are on (irrigation_unlimited.disable, which IU keeps across a restart), then switches on the imported schedules that IU had on. A sequence or zone schedule that IU runs switched off, or whose controller is off, stays off here too. A zone that IU runs switched off inside a sequence is named on the page: IU leaves it out, but here its step waters it until you switch that step off. If the import has no record of which schedules IU had on (an import from before this was kept), none of that program's schedules comes on and the page says so: switch them on yourself, or go back, import again and switch over again. IU is switched off first, so for a moment nothing waters rather than both.
  • Go back to Irrigation Unlimited switches the imported schedules off first, then on again the controllers the switch turned off, and no others. Which schedules were on is kept: switching over again brings back those, including your own changes.
  • If a step fails, the one before it is undone, and the page says who waters.
  • Who waters is read from what is on, not from the buttons: if IU switches a controller on again (by hand, or because IU does not restore its state) while imported schedules are on, or you switch a schedule on by hand while IU waters, the page says that both would water and offers to switch IU off. It also says when nothing waters.
  • What still uses Irrigation Unlimited lists your automations and scripts that name IU's services, events (irrigation_unlimited_start, _finish, …) or entities, with a link to each. An adjust-time automation has nothing left to do: the steps are calculated here. Nothing is changed for you.

After the switch, importing again keeps the on or off you gave each schedule, and a schedule new to the import comes with IU's own on and off, since IU no longer waters.

docs.title: What the import does not carry over
docs.text:
• A controller with a master becomes a supply, and its programs water beside the other controllers', as in IU. Controllers without a master share the mains: their programs run one after the other.
  • Runs that IU overlapped run one after the other.
  • A step's repeat becomes passes: the water in parts with a soak between, not full runs.
  • entity_states, threshold, a zone's default duration for manual runs, the master's check_back and volume, an unbounded cron, a sun event other than sunrise and sunset.

docs.title: By hand
docs.text:
If you would rather rebuild than import:

  1. Choose Calculate and water in Settings › General.
  2. Add your pump or main valve under Watering › Pumps and valves, and pick it in each zone.
  3. Make a program per IU sequence: its steps are the sequence's zones, in order. Leave the duration on calculated.
  4. Add a schedule to each. If IU ran it to finish at sunrise, take Sunrise, must be done.
  5. Switch IU's own schedules off, and remove the two automations that handed it durations and reset the water balance.
  6. Look at Watering › Planning: it shows the next days (3, 7 or 14, as you pick on the chart). Compare it with what IU would have done before you remove IU.

docs.title: Not in Smart Irrigation
docs.text:
• Cron schedules (the import expands a bounded one into time schedules).
  • Several independent controllers, each with its own sequences. Several supplies are possible, and each zone picks its own, but there is one program queue.
  • Overlap of whole programs: only the steps of one program can overlap (negative wait), never two programs.
  • An adjustable granularity, renaming the entities IU creates, a built-in simulator.
  • IU's entity_states choice of which commands a timed valve receives.

docs.title: Not in Irrigation Unlimited
docs.text:
• A water model: evapotranspiration, a water balance per zone, and a water balance credit for the water that really went through.
  • Durations calculated from the weather, instead of typed.
  • Weather skip conditions (rain, frost, wind, wet soil) that can be set per schedule.
  • Hardware dead-man arming (MQTT or ZHA) and a check that a valve did not close by itself while it should be open.

docs.title: Watering with programs
docs.text:
Smart Irrigation can water in two ways, and you pick one in Settings › General, under What Smart Irrigation does (the setup assistant asks too):

  • Calculate and water: Smart Irrigation runs the whole watering itself. Programs of steps say which zones water and in what order, their schedules say when ("done by sunrise", every other day, only in summer, after another program), and pumps and main valves come on with the zones they feed. This page is about that mode.
  • Calculate only, the choice of a new installation: Smart Irrigation works out how long each zone needs and something of yours opens the valves, an automation, a controller or another integration.

docs.title: Turning it on
docs.text:
Choose Calculate and water in Settings › General, in the first card's list, What Smart Irrigation does. There is no other switch to turn on.

Choosing it:

  • lets Smart Irrigation open and close the valves itself, and turns on observed watering, so a watering by hand counts too;
  • waters with programs, each one the zones of its steps, started by its own schedules. When there is no program yet, it creates one with the zones that have a valve and a schedule that starts it as your start trigger did (done by sunrise by default), so nothing changes in when you water. A zone added later is watered once a program has it in a step: the setup assistant puts a new zone in one for you;
  • adds a Watering tab to the panel, with three pages: Planning, Programs, and Pumps and valves. The cards below are in it.

Choosing Calculate only goes back to calculating for an automation of your own: Smart Irrigation fires its start event at the start trigger and opens no valve. Your programs and supplies stay stored for the day you choose Calculate and water again.

Coming from 2026.11.0 or earlier

Up to 2026.11.0 this took two switches, Full controller and Let Smart Irrigation control the valve, and the main program of that time could also be started by the start trigger or switched off on its own. An installation is moved over once, keeping its watering as it was: direct valve control alone becomes Calculate and water, the active start trigger becomes a schedule of the program that was the main program, now an ordinary program called Watering (see below; the other triggers you had defined become schedules switched off, so none is lost: switch one on to use it), and if it was switched off its schedules stay switched off.

No main program any more (2026.11.1). Up to 2026.11.0 a special main program watered every zone with a valve, in the order of the general settings, and the other programs had steps. Now every program is the same kind. Your main program was turned once into an ordinary program, so it waters exactly as before: it keeps its id main (its sensor, its last runs and its notifications stay) and its schedules, and its name unless it was still the default Main program, which becomes Watering in the language of Home Assistant (a name you changed is kept); and gets explicit steps, the zones it watered in the same order. With one after the other, one step per zone, each followed by the pause between zones as its wait (none after the last); with all at once, one step with all the zones. Each step takes the calculated duration, in the passes the old setting asked for. A zone added afterwards is not watered until a program has it in a step. The Program on setting and its switch entity are gone too: a program starts on its own through the schedules that are on, so a program that was off had its schedules switched off. Run now always works. The set_program_enabled action is deprecated and will be removed in 2027.11: it still works, switching all of a program's schedules on or off, and raises a repair notice; use set_schedule_enabled instead.

One thing is different from the moment it is on: a valve found open at startup that no run of ours owns is closed. After a crash or a restart, a valve left open by a run nobody resumes would water until someone noticed. A reading that says nothing (unavailable, unknown) is never taken for an open valve. That startup alignment also closes a zone's extra valves, and it looks at the supplies: a pump or main valve that is on while nothing holds it is switched off, and one whose state cannot be read yet is looked at again 30 and 120 seconds later, since its entity often comes up after Home Assistant has started.

docs.title: Pumps and main valves (supplies)
docs.text:
A supply is one or several entities, a pump or a main valve in front of the zone valves, that run while a zone they feed is being watered. Add them on the Pumps and main valves card, under Watering › Pumps and valves, then pick one in each zone's Pump or main valve.

Each supply has two delays, in seconds, and both are signed, from -3600 to +3600:

Positive Negative Delay before The supply comes on that long before the zone valve opens. The valve opens first, and the supply comes on that long after. Delay after The supply stays on that long after the zone valve closes. The supply goes off that long before the valve closes, so a pump never pushes against a closed valve.

Power cut before starting (kick_seconds, 0 to 60, 0 by default; advanced mode, shown in every mode once it is not 0): for a pump whose pressure controller only starts again after its power has been cut, the supply is switched off that many seconds and then on, each time it is switched on. A supply already on for another zone is not cut again.

A supply is on while anything holds it, and goes off when the last hold is given back, after its delay. It is never switched off on a guess of when the cycle will end. Two zones in a row share one run of the pump, and with a delay after the pump stays on between them.

A supply that will not come on keeps the zone shut. Each switch call is tried twice, 3 seconds apart, and the entity must then read a state within 5 seconds. If the supply still has not come on, the zone's valve is not opened (no pump, no water), the run of that zone ends with a smart_irrigation_zone_problem of reason supply_did_not_turn_on, and smart_irrigation_supply_problem is fired too. A supply that will not go off never blocks anything: the off is tried again after 15, 45 and 120 seconds, smart_irrigation_supply_problem (reason supply_did_not_turn_off) is fired for the first failure (the retries are silent), and a supply still on after that stays recorded as on, so the next run or the next startup puts it off. The payload of supply_problem is supply_id, supply, entity_id and reason (supply_did_not_turn_on or supply_did_not_turn_off).

A zone can also have other valves of the zone that open and close with its own (a zone whose water comes through two valves), and light and cover entities are accepted as valves.

docs.title: Programs
docs.text:
A program is an ordered list of steps. A step is one zone, or several zones watered at the same time. By default a step takes the duration Smart Irrigation calculated for each zone, which is what sets this apart from a timer.

For each step:

  • Duration: calculated by Smart Irrigation (the default), calculated times a percentage (110 % in a heat wave, 50 % for a plant that needs less), or fixed (seconds of water). The lead time that fills the pipe is kept in every mode. A zone that needs no water gets none, unless the step is fixed.
  • Only water when the deficit is at least (min_deficit_mm, 0 to 100, 0 means none; YAML only, for instance min_deficit_mm: 7 on the step, see YAML-only options): a zone is only watered by the step when its water deficit (how far its water balance is below zero, in mm) is at least this. A zone under it sits the step out; this is only written in the log (reason below_deficit), not exposed anywhere else. It applies to calculated and percent steps; a fixed step is always watered. Set, it replaces the zone's own irrigation threshold for this step: a zone whose threshold of 20 mm has not been reached yet, at a deficit of 15 mm, is still watered by a step asking for 7 mm, for the run its water balance implies.
  • Minimum water, Maximum water and Time added (+) or removed (-) (min_seconds, max_seconds, adjust_seconds): the water of a step is raised to the minimum or capped at the maximum (0 means none, at most 86400 seconds each), and the time added or removed is a signed number of seconds (-6 h to +6 h). The time added or removed (adjust_seconds) is YAML only, for instance adjust_seconds: -120 on the step (see YAML-only options). A minimum never turns a zone that needs no water into watering: a calculated duration of zero stays zero. The lead time is added on top of these bounds. The order is below.
  • Fixed seconds (seconds, for a fixed step): at most 86400.
  • Percentage (for a percent step): 0 to 1000.
  • Water in several passes: the step's water is split into this many passes, 1 to 6, each zone soaking between two of them for the soak time, one setting for every program, shown next to the step's passes (cycle and soak).
  • Wait after this step: seconds before the next step, from -3600 to +21600. Empty is no wait. A negative wait overlaps the steps: the next one starts that many seconds before this one ends, so the valves and the pump of both are open together for that time (up to an hour, and never longer than this step runs).
  • Volume limit: a zone stops once its water meter has counted this many litres, at most 100000. The meter reports every so often, so it is not exact. A zone without a meter ignores it.

For the program:

  • Rounds (tours, YAML only, for instance tours: 2 at the top of the program, see YAML-only options): the whole list is watered this many times (1 to 6), each round with its share of the water. Unlike passes, which repeat a step before going on, a round waters every step once and starts again, so each zone soaks while the others water and no soak time is needed.

Any program can be deleted, the one with the id main included, except the last one: the panel shows no Delete button then, and a save that would leave no program is refused. To stop it watering, switch its schedules off.

How the duration of a step is worked out, in this order: the step's percentage (percent steps), then the percentage of an adjust_program adjustment in force, then the step's time added or removed plus the seconds of that adjustment, then the minimum, then the maximum (so when the minimum is larger than the maximum, the maximum wins). Nothing under zero is watered. These bounds apply to the total water of the step, before it is split across the rounds; the lead time comes on top of each pass.

One queue per supply. Programs whose zones share a supply take turns: a different program asked for while one runs waits its turn, and a manual run asked for during a program is added behind it. Zones without a supply share one queue, the mains, so an installation without supplies runs one program at a time. A program on the well pump and one on the mains share nothing and water side by side. A program waits for every supply its steps name (all of its zones, not only those the plan will water), and the runs that asked first go first on every supply, so one that needs two supplies is not overtaken by runs that need one. A one-off run of every zone waits for everything else, and everything else waits for it. A zone watered by hand (water_zone) waits only for its own supply. Pause, resume and Stop act on every run; Next step moves every program on, or one with program_id. A program that is already running or waiting is not queued a second time: run_program on it is ignored (with a line in the log), and so is a schedule that comes due meanwhile. The plan is worked out when the turn comes, from the zones as they are then: a zone watered meanwhile is not watered again.

docs.title: Seeing a program before it runs
docs.text: An unfolded program shows what a run would do: one line per zone on a time axis, its passes as bars, the time its pipe fills in a lighter shade and the soak between two passes hatched. Two zones of one step run side by side, a negative wait shows the next step starting before the last one ends, and the total is at the end of the axis. The durations are the ones Smart Irrigation would water now; they follow the weather, so a run may differ when it starts. The Planning page draws each run it lists, on the clock.

docs.title: A program in YAML
docs.text:
Edit in YAML (the { } icon of a program) shows the program as text, in place of the form, and the same icon brings the form back. A program written in YAML is an ordinary program once applied, and the form edits it as any other. To paste a program written elsewhere, add a New program and open it in YAML.

Nothing is saved until Apply. As you type, the program is cleaned the way a save cleans it and drawn on the timeline, and a zone that does not exist, or that the run leaves out (no valve, or disabled), is named. Only a valid program can be applied.

The text is short on purpose, so it can be read, copied between installations or written by an assistant. What is left out takes its default, the same as the form: a calculated duration, one pass, no wait, a schedule that starts at its moment every day with the weather taken into account.

A simple programDone by sunrise, then a chained programWith options only YAML sets 
name: Evening
steps:
  - zones: [Vegetable garden, Greenhouse]   # watered together
    mode: percent
    percent: 80
    passes: 2                               # cycle and soak
  - zones: [Hedges]
    delay: -60                              # the next step starts a minute early
schedules:
  - time: "21:00"
    weekdays: [0, 2, 4]                     # 0 is Monday

name: Lawn
steps:
  - zones: [Front lawn]
  - zones: [Back lawn]
schedules:
  - type: sun
    event: sunrise
    anchor: end                             # done by sunrise
    every_n_days: 2

name: Greenhouse drip
steps:
  - zones: [Greenhouse]
    mode: fixed
    seconds: 600
schedules:
  - type: after
    after_program: Lawn                     # 15 minutes after Lawn
    offset_minutes: 15
    weather: false                          # waters whatever the weather

name: Summer beds
tours: 2                                    # the whole list, twice
steps:
  - zones: [Roses, Shrubs]
    adjust_seconds: 120                     # two more minutes each
    min_deficit_mm: 5                       # only when 5 mm short or more
schedules:
  - time: "06:00"
    months: [5, 6, 7, 8, 9]                 # May to September
    parity: even                            # even days of the month
    skip_conditions: [freeze, wind]         # only these weather checks

A step names its zones by name (case aside) or by number; a name two zones share is not guessed, use the number. The id lines keep a program, a step or a schedule the same one across an edit (a schedule remembers its last run under its id): keep them when you edit, leave them out of a new program.

YAML-only options

As in Home Assistant's own visual editors, some options have no field in the form, even when they are set: they are written here, in YAML (or by the services or an assistant). Editing the program in the form keeps them as they are, and an unfolded program that uses one says so at its top, in a Set in YAML (not editable here) box listing them, with Edit in YAML at hand to change them. They are:

  • for the program: tours: 2, the rounds;
  • for a step: adjust_seconds: -120, the time added or removed, and min_deficit_mm: 7, only water when the deficit is at least;
  • for a schedule: every_offset: 1, the shift of every N days, parity: even (or odd), days_of_month: [1, 15, last] and months: [5, 6, 7, 8, 9], the days; fallback_time: previous (or "06:00"), for polar day and night; skip_conditions: [rain_sensor, freeze], only some of the checks (the Take the weather into account switch itself stays in the form).
  • for a zone, in its own Edit in YAML: safety_off_state_key: state_l1, the safety off state key, and open_resends: 0, how often the open is sent again.

Every key, with its values and default. The same reference is given to assistants, which can write and check a program for you.

docs.title: Program
docs.text: Key Values Default What it does name string The name shown to the user. steps list of step The steps, watered in this order (see step). schedules list of schedule [] When it starts (see schedule). All off or none: it starts only when run by hand. tours 1 to 6 1 YAML only. How many times the whole list of steps is gone through in one run. notify notify Who is told about its runs, and when (see notify). Absent: nobody.

docs.title: Step
docs.text: Key Values Default What it does zones list of zone id or name The zones of the step, watered together. Names are matched to ids. mode calculated, percent, fixed calculated How long it waters: the duration Smart Irrigation calculated, a percent of it, or a fixed number of seconds. percent 0 to 1000 % 100 With mode percent: the share of the calculated water. seconds 0 to 86400 s 0 With mode fixed: the seconds of water. passes 1 to 6 1 Cycle and soak: the water split in this many passes, with the soak of the settings between them. delay -3600 to 21600 s Wait after this step before the next one; negative: the next one starts that long before this one ends (overlap). max_litres 0 to 100000 L 0 A zone stops once this many litres went through its flow meter (0: no limit). enabled boolean true false: the step is left out of the runs. min_seconds 0 to 86400 s 0 Least water of a zone in the step (0: no bound). max_seconds 0 to 86400 s 0 Most water of a zone in the step (0: no bound). adjust_seconds -21600 to 21600 s 0 YAML only. Seconds added to (or, negative, taken from) the water, after the percent and before the bounds. min_deficit_mm 0 to 100 mm 0 YAML only. A zone whose water deficit is below this sits the step out (0: the zone's own threshold). Not for mode fixed.

docs.text: Key Values Default What it does enabled boolean true false: this schedule starts nothing. type time, sun, after time time: at a clock time; sun: at a sun event with an offset; after: when another program has really watered and finished, or at its planned moment when it did not water (held back, suspended, nothing to water); not when it was stopped by hand or failed. time string HH:MM 06:00 The clock time. (time only) event sunrise, sunset, azimuth sunrise The sun event; azimuth: when the sun reaches azimuth. (sun only) offset_minutes -720 to 720 min 0 sun: minutes after the event (negative: before). after: minutes after the other program finished, or after its planned moment when it did not water (0 or more). No loops. Shifts the every-N-days cycle by that many days, to take turns (groups A, B, C). parity any, even, odd any YAML only. Even or odd days of the month only. days_of_month 1 to 31 [] YAML only.
